title: shipyard configuration
description: config.toml for shipyard, the macOS menu bar app for the pull requests, issues and workflow runs on your projects. The file lives in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shipyard/ (default ~/.config/shipyard/). Every key is optional; a missing key takes its default, so an empty file means defaults with no projects. Keys are kebab-case. Shipyard applies edits live, keeps the last valid configuration when an edit is broken, and ignores unknown keys with a warning.

version.description: The configuration format version. Only 1 exists.

refresh-interval-seconds.description: How often to refresh, in seconds. A floor: shipyard stretches it when a refresh at this interval would spend more than max-share-percent of a GitHub rate limit.

launch-at-login.description: Start shipyard when you log in.

hide-authors.description: Logins whose items are hidden, e.g. "dependabot[bot]".

menu-bar.description: What the menu bar shows next to the icon.

count.description: The attention count: one total, split by kind (pull requests, issues, runs), or no number.

menu.description: How the panel draws your projects.

layout.description: One scrolling list of every project, one line per item under pinned project headers, or one project at a time in tabs.

rate-limit.description: How much of your GitHub rate limit shipyard may use, and whether the panel shows it. The limit is shared with every other tool using your account, your agents included.

show.description: Show the rate limit in the panel footer always, only when it's low (below 25%), or never.

max-share-percent.description: The largest share of each hourly GitHub limit (GraphQL points, REST requests) shipyard spends, in percent.

attention.description: Which reasons make an open item need attention (count in the menu bar). Clicking an item clears all of them until it changes again. Closed items never need attention.

unseen.description: An item you haven't clicked yet.

changed.description: An item that changed (commits, comments, reviews, checks, review request) since you clicked it.

review-requested.description: A pull request that requests your review.

checks-failed.description: A pull request whose checks failed.

defaults.description: What every project shows and notifies about, unless the project overrides it.

notifications.description: The notification rules for every project that doesn't list its own. Default: a new pull request by anyone.

projects.description: One [[projects]] block per project, shown as a section in this order.

project.description: A named group of one or more GitHub repositories, shown as one section. Tables here merge key by key onto [defaults]; notifications replaces the default list.

name.description: The section's title; unique across projects.

repositories.description: The project's repositories as owner/name slugs, each listed once. Shipyard also rejects two spellings that differ only in case, which this check can't see.

notifications.description: This project's notification rules; replaces [[defaults.notifications]]. An empty list means no notifications for this project.

pull-requests.description: Pull requests from anyone: open ones, then those closed within the closed window, newest first.

closed-window-days.description: How many days closed and merged pull requests stay listed; 0 hides them.

issues.description: Issues from anyone: open ones, then those closed within the closed window.

closed-window-days.description: How many days closed issues stay listed; 0 hides them.

workflow-runs.description: GitHub Actions runs: running now, plus finished within the finished window.

finished-window-hours.description: How many hours finished runs stay listed; 0 hides them.

branches.description: Which branches' runs to list: the default branch and open pull request branches, or all branches.

notifications.description: Notification rules: a macOS notification is sent for an event when a rule names it and its author filter matches.

authors.description: Whose items: anyone, you (me), anyone but you and bots (others), or bots (a Bot account or a [bot] login).
